events.title: Commodore 128 was released
events.text: Commodore 128 was released. Based on a complex multi-mode architecture, this was Commodore's last 8-bit computer. Cost: $299.95 for each of the CPU unit and accompanying 1571 disk drive. (US)

events.text: Meiko Scientific formed.

events.title: PostScript introduced by Adobe Systems
events.text: PostScript introduced by Adobe Systems. It is a powerful page description language used in the Apple Laserwriter printer. Adopted by IBM for their use in March 1987. (US)

events.title: Apple released another enhanced version of the Macintosh (the Macintos
events.text: Apple released another enhanced version of the Macintosh (the Macintosh Plus personal computer)this one could cope with 4 MB of RAM (for the first time, upgradable via SIMMs) and it had a built-in SCSI adapter based on the NCR 5380. (US)

events.title: Compaq Deskpro 386 was released and is the first implementation of the
events.text: Compaq Deskpro 386 was released and is the first implementation of the 80386 processor in a computer system for sale to the public. (US)

events.title: AD-LIB soundcard released
events.text: AD-LIB soundcard released. Not widely supported until a software company, Taito, released several games fully supporting AD-LIBthe word then spread how much the special sound effects and music enhanced the games. (Canada)

events.text: HyperCard software released.

events.text: MCGA released (only for low end PS/2s, i.e. the Model 30) by IBM.

events.title: On April 2 PS/2 Systems were introduced by IBM
events.text: On April 2 PS/2 Systems were introduced by IBM. The first 4 models were released on this date. The PS/2 Model 30 based on an 8086 processor and an old XT bus, Models 50 and 60 based on the 80286 processor and the Model 80 based on the 80386 processor

events.title: Adobe Photoshop software created
events.text: Adobe Photoshop software created.

events.title: Macintosh IIx released
events.text: Macintosh IIx released. It was based on a new processor, the Motorola 68030. It still ran at 16 MHz but now achieved 3.9 MIPS. It could be expanded to 128 MB of RAM and had 6 NuBus expansions slots.

events.title: 80486DX released by Intel
events.text: 80486DX released by Intel. It contains the equivalent of about 1.2 million transistors. At the time of release the fastest version ran at 25 MHz and achieved up to 20 MIPS. (US)

events.title: Open Architecture System Integration Strategy is presented by Apple Co
events.text: Open Architecture System Integration Strategy is presented by Apple Computer as the philosophy behind the Mac in marketing beginning in 1989.

events.title: Tim Berners-Lee submitted a memorandum, titled "Information Management
events.text: Tim Berners-Lee submitted a memorandum, titled "Information Management: A Proposal" to the management at CERN. The proposal talks of "... a "web" of notes with links (like references) between them ...". (Switzerland)
